sources: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard
PCAF Global GHG Accounting Standard for Financial Industry (2022)
WRI/WBCSD Scope 3 calculation guidance by sector
metadata.notes: Typical percentages are indicative ranges based on published sector analyses and CDP disclosures. Actual values vary significantly by company. Materiality ratings follow GHG Protocol significance thresholds: High (>10% of expected total Scope 3), Medium (3-10%), Low (<3%), NA (not applicable to sector). Percentages may not sum to exactly 100% due to rounding and sector variability.

manufacturing_general.label: Manufacturing (General)
manufacturing_general.description: Broad manufacturing sector including discrete and process manufacturing, excluding food/beverage and textiles which have dedicated profiles.

1_purchased_goods.notes: Largest category. Raw materials and components dominate. Prioritize top 20 suppliers for supplier-specific data.

2_capital_goods.notes: Machinery, equipment, buildings. Lumpy year-over-year. Report in year of purchase.

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT and T&D losses. Straightforward using Scope 1/2 consumption data with WTT factors.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Inbound logistics. Need weight, distance, and transport mode data from procurement/logistics.

5_waste.notes: By waste type and treatment method. Often available from waste management contracts.

6_business_travel.notes: Air, rail, hotel. Often available from travel management company or expense system.

7_employee_commuting.notes: Employee survey for mode split and distance. National averages as fallback.

8_upstream_leased.notes: Only if significant leased assets not in Scope 1/2. Depends on consolidation approach.

9_downstream_transport.notes: Outbound logistics to customer. Similar method to Cat 4.

10_processing_sold_products.notes: Only for intermediate products. Estimate downstream processing energy requirements.

11_use_of_sold_products.notes: Highly variable. Dominant for energy-using products. Based on product specs and usage patterns.

12_end_of_life.notes: End-of-life treatment of products sold. Based on material composition and treatment assumptions.

14_franchises.notes: Only applicable if company operates a franchise model.

15_investments.notes: Only material if company holds significant financial investments or joint ventures.

food_beverage.label: Food & Beverage
food_beverage.description: Food processing, beverage production, and agricultural product companies. Agricultural supply chain emissions (land use change, livestock, fertilizer) drive high Cat 1.

1_purchased_goods.notes: Agricultural inputs, ingredients, packaging. Land use change and farming emissions are dominant. Use sector-specific factors (e.g., ecoinvent agri-food).

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT for fuels used in processing and cold chain.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Inbound logistics including cold chain. Temperature-controlled transport has higher factors.

5_waste.notes: Food waste in operations, packaging waste. Organic waste to landfill has high methane emissions.

6_business_travel.notes: Generally low relative to supply chain emissions.

7_employee_commuting.notes: Factory and office workers. Often estimated using national averages.

9_downstream_transport.notes: Distribution to retailers including refrigerated transport.

10_processing_sold_products.notes: Relevant for ingredient suppliers whose products are further processed.

11_use_of_sold_products.notes: Refrigeration at consumer, cooking energy. Relevant for frozen/chilled products.

12_end_of_life.notes: Packaging end-of-life, food waste at consumer. Growing scrutiny under EPR regulations.

14_franchises.notes: Significant for restaurant/fast-food franchise models. Energy use per franchise location.

15_investments.notes: Joint ventures in agricultural supply chains may be relevant.

fashion_textiles.label: Fashion & Textiles
fashion_textiles.description: Apparel, footwear, and textile manufacturing. Raw material production (cotton, synthetics) and garment manufacturing in supply chain dominate emissions.

1_purchased_goods.notes: Raw fibers, fabrics, dyes, trims. Synthetic fibers (polyester from petrochemicals) and cotton (water/pesticide intensive) are key. Use textile-specific LCA databases.

2_capital_goods.notes: Retail fixtures, warehouse equipment, IT systems.

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT for store and warehouse energy.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Often global supply chains with long-distance shipping. Sea freight dominant but air freight for fast fashion.

5_waste.notes: Cutting waste, defective goods, packaging. Pre-consumer textile waste.

6_business_travel.notes: Travel to suppliers, trade shows, retail operations.

7_employee_commuting.notes: Retail staff, office, and warehouse workers.

8_upstream_leased.notes: Leased retail locations if not in Scope 1/2.

9_downstream_transport.notes: Distribution to stores and e-commerce deliveries. Last-mile e-commerce growing.

10_processing_sold_products.notes: Relevant for fabric/yarn suppliers whose products are further processed.

11_use_of_sold_products.notes: Consumer washing, drying, ironing over garment lifetime. Significant for fast-fashion with high wash frequency.

12_end_of_life.notes: Textile waste largely to landfill or incineration. Low recycling rates for blended fibers. Growing EPR requirements.

14_franchises.notes: Relevant for brands with franchise retail model.

energy_utilities.label: Energy & Utilities
energy_utilities.description: Electricity generation, oil & gas, natural gas distribution, and water utilities. Cat 11 (use of sold products) dominates for fossil fuel sellers; Cat 3 is significant for all.

1_purchased_goods.notes: Fuels purchased for resale (if not Cat 11), equipment, chemicals for water treatment.

2_capital_goods.notes: Power plants, turbines, pipelines, grid infrastructure. Large and lumpy.

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT of fuels used in generation, T&D losses. Very significant for fossil fuel generators.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Transport of fuels (coal, gas, biomass) to generation sites.

5_waste.notes: Ash disposal (coal plants), general operational waste.

9_downstream_transport.notes: Fuel distribution to end users (pipelines, tankers).

10_processing_sold_products.notes: Energy is a final product, not intermediate.

11_use_of_sold_products.notes: Combustion of sold fuels (natural gas, LPG, oil products) by end users. Dominant category for fossil fuel companies. Calculate as: volume sold x combustion emission factor.

12_end_of_life.notes: Decommissioning of sold equipment (e.g., boilers, meters).

15_investments.notes: Joint ventures in energy projects, equity investments in other energy companies.

construction.label: Construction
construction.description: Building construction, civil engineering, and construction materials. Embodied carbon in materials (Cat 1) and operational carbon of buildings delivered (Cat 11) dominate.

1_purchased_goods.notes: Cement, steel, concrete, glass, insulation, timber. Use EPDs where available. CBAM relevant for imported steel and cement.

2_capital_goods.notes: Heavy machinery, cranes, vehicles. High absolute value but relatively stable year-over-year.

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT for diesel used on construction sites and offices.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Heavy materials transport (concrete, steel, aggregates). Short distances but high weight.

5_waste.notes: Construction and demolition waste. High volume. Increasingly regulated for recycling rates.

7_employee_commuting.notes: Site workers, office staff. Multiple site locations complicate surveys.

9_downstream_transport.notes: Delivery of finished products/components to project sites.

10_processing_sold_products.notes: Relevant for building material manufacturers (e.g., concrete mixed on site).

11_use_of_sold_products.notes: Operational energy of buildings delivered over their design lifetime (30-60 years). Increasingly important as whole-life carbon assessments become standard.

12_end_of_life.notes: Demolition of buildings at end of life. Long time horizon makes this uncertain.

13_downstream_leased.notes: If company leases out built properties.

financial_services.label: Financial Services
financial_services.description: Banks, insurance, asset management, private equity. Category 15 (Investments / financed emissions) overwhelmingly dominates, often 70-95% of total Scope 3.

1_purchased_goods.notes: IT equipment, office supplies, professional services. Relatively small vs financed emissions.

3_fuel_energy_related.notes: WTT for office energy. Small relative to financed emissions.

4_upstream_transport.notes: Service company — minimal physical goods transport.

5_waste.notes: Office waste only. Immaterial relative to financed emissions.

6_business_travel.notes: Significant for client-facing roles. Often well-tracked via travel management systems.

7_employee_commuting.notes: Office workers. Remote work policies reduce this.

8_upstream_leased.notes: Leased office space (common in financial services). May be Scope 1/2 depending on consolidation.

13_downstream_leased.notes: Properties leased to tenants. Relevant for banks with real estate portfolios.

15_investments.notes: Financed emissions — THE dominant category. Follow PCAF methodology by asset class (listed equity, bonds, loans, project finance, commercial real estate, mortgages). Increasingly required by regulators (ECB, PRA) and CSRD.
